EmailTemplate.subject: New Health Screening Devices
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear <BPL name>,
We are excited to announce that the American Red Cross will soon begin trialing in select areas two new FDA-approved health screening devices to improve the blood donation experience.
What’s new? Measuring hemoglobin levels: This new device eliminates the fingerstick and instead utilizes an OrSense ring-shaped sensor that is fitted onto an individual’s finger to measure their hemoglobin levels. This method provides a quick measurement of the donor's blood components, while greatly improving the donor's comfort.
Measuring temperature, blood pressure and pulse rate: This new device replaces traditional manual devices and instead utilizes an automated Masimo device to measure individuals’ temperature, blood pressure, and pulse rate.
Preview the devices in action < unlisted YouTube page link provided by 3/5/24>
What else should my donors know? · By transitioning to these devices, the Red Cross helps achieve its goal of reducing its impact on the environment by significantly reducing the use of disposable medical supplies. · Good blood circulation in the hands is important for the most accurate results--the Red Cross suggest donors try to keep their hands as warm as possible while waiting to give blood.
If your donors have questions about their eligibility, please refer them to our Red Cross Donor and Client Support Center at 1-866-236-3276, option 1.
Our top priority is the health of all our donors and recipients. We are so grateful for your continued support as a Blood Program Leader, and we look forward to trialing these new devices at one of your upcoming blood drives.
Thank you for being a community leader and bringing people together to help save lives!
Sincerely,
<Red Cross Representative>
Ps. While these devices may not appear at all drives, there is a chance they may be trialed during your operation.
